squawks.headline: Losses on the BoE's quantitative tightening for 2027-28 are put at £5.7bn more than forecast in March
squawks.detail: The higher estimate of losses on the Bank of England's QT programme for 2027-28 was reported on Budget day. It is £5.7bn above the March forecast.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Europeans will not join the trilateral Ukraine talks and a date will be announced soon
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said European representatives are not being invited to the negotiations on Ukraine, Interfax reported. The Kremlin also said the date of the trilateral talks would be announced soon.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada signals further hikes may be needed and raises its inflation forecasts to 2.9% for 2026 and 3.1% for 2027
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's Monetary Policy Report now puts inflation at 2.9% in 2026 (2.5% in July), 3.1% in 2027 (2.0%) and 2.2% in 2028 (2.1%), above target until mid-2028. It assumes Brent averages around $100 in Q4 before easing to around $75 by end-2028. Governor Macklem said the hike was meant to stop high energy prices spreading into wider inflation, that rates may have to rise again and that the council will go carefully, deciding one meeting at a time.

squawks.headline: OBR says the government's council housebuilding ambition could cost an extra £3bn-£4bn a year
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility put this estimate on the council housebuilding plans in its Budget documents.

squawks.headline: OBR expects the Employment Rights Act to have a negative economic impact
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility gave this assessment of the Employment Rights Act alongside the Budget. No figures were reported.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada raises its key rate by 25bp to 2.5%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada lifted its key rate to 2.5% from 2.25%, matching the 2.5% forecast. It is the bank's first rate rise in three years.

squawks.headline: UK plans to extend its forthcoming carbon border tax to refined products, Treasury documents show
squawks.detail: Treasury Budget documents show the government plans to widen the scope of its upcoming carbon border tax to cover refined products.

squawks.headline: OBR says headroom would be £10.2bn if fuel duty stayed frozen; cumulative cost of freezes and 5p cut reaches £139bn
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget documents put headroom at £10.2bn if fuel duty had stayed frozen. It also says the cumulative cost of fuel duty freezes and the 5p cut has risen to £139bn.

squawks.headline: OBR puts the chance of meeting the fiscal mandate at 56%, down from 59% at Budget 2025
squawks.detail: The OBR also says the Budget plans slow the near-term pace of fiscal consolidation compared with the previous plans.

squawks.headline: OBR expects the UK tax-to-GDP ratio to pass its 37.2% record in 2027-28 and keep rising
squawks.detail: The OBR says the ratio rises in every year of the forecast. It also expects the bank tax increase to bring in £1bn in receipts in 2027-28.

squawks.headline: OBR raises 2026-27 UK borrowing forecast to £133.2bn from £115.5bn, and 2027-28 to £112bn from £96.5bn
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget forecast puts government borrowing at £68.3bn in 2031-32. Net borrowing over 2026-31 is reported as £65bn higher than in the previous forecast.

squawks.headline: European benchmark gas price hits €100/MWh, its first time at that level since December 2022
squawks.detail: The European benchmark gas price is reported reaching €100/MWh, a level last seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

squawks.headline: OBR expects UK CPI inflation to peak at 3.75% on a quarterly basis in early 2027
squawks.detail: The quarterly peak is in the OBR's central forecast, published alongside the Budget.

squawks.headline: OBR cuts headroom against the debt rule to £24bn from £27.1bn
squawks.detail: The OBR says Budget policies add £3.5bn to borrowing in 2027-28 and cut it by £11.7bn in 2031-32. Reported calculations show £65bn more borrowing over 2026-27 to 2030-31 than in the March forecast.

squawks.headline: OBR raises UK inflation forecast to 3.1% for 2026 and 3.5% for 2027
squawks.detail: The OBR's Economic and Fiscal Outlook puts 2026 inflation at 3.1%, up from 2.3%, and 2027 inflation at 3.5% in its central forecast, up from 2% in March.

squawks.headline: OBR calls fiscal margins very small and says a 1% rate move shifts debt interest by £16bn
squawks.detail: The OBR describes the UK fiscal position as very challenging and says a higher, longer energy price peak could lift 2027-28 borrowing £17bn above its central forecast. It adds that productivity growth 0.5 percentage points higher or lower could leave borrowing £50bn lower or £40bn higher.

squawks.headline: DMO cuts long conventional syndication to £12.5bn and raises index-linked syndication to £7.8bn for 2026-27
squawks.detail: The revised DMO remit sets long-dated conventional gilt syndications at £12.5bn, down from £15bn in April. Index-linked syndications rise to £7.8bn from £7bn, and index-linked auctions fall to £15.6bn from £16bn.

squawks.headline: World Bank forecasts global energy prices up 32% in 2026, a four-year high, on Middle East war
squawks.detail: The World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026 and overall commodity prices to rise 23% before falling 7% in 2027. It warns that further Middle East escalation or damage to Russian oil infrastructure could lift energy prices further.

squawks.headline: DMO sets 2026-27 gross gilt issuance at £250.6bn, above the £249.6bn poll and the April remit of £246.2bn
squawks.detail: The UK Debt Management Office published its revised 2026-27 financing remit alongside the Budget. Planned gross gilt issuance is £250.6bn, compared with £249.6bn expected in a poll and £246.2bn in the April remit.

squawks.headline: Healey takes total government backing for council homes to £40bn and makes land sold to social housing providers VAT-free
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey also announced £1.5bn for a social and affordable housing programme. He said all land sold to social housing providers will be free of VAT.

squawks.headline: Healey sets a target of 3% of GDP for UK defence spending in 2030
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey gave the target for UK defence spending during his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Healey replaces the lifetime ISA with a first-time buyer ISA and gives £4.7bn to a 'Your first home' scheme
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced both measures in his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Canadian official says trade talks with the US have made limited progress
squawks.detail: Reuters cited a Canadian government official familiar with the talks, speaking on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Budget sets up a defence finance taskforce, with the National Wealth Fund and National Bank deploying up to £5bn on defence
squawks.detail: Healey said the government will start treaty talks with Finland, Poland and the Netherlands on a multilateral defence mechanism and will set out how it meets its NATO defence commitment. The National Wealth Fund and the National Bank will put up to £5bn of funding and investment into the defence industrial base.

squawks.headline: Healey commits £10bn more in support for Ukraine in the Budget
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced a further £10bn of support for Ukraine and said Britain would back Ukraine for as long as needed.

squawks.headline: Healey says triple lock changes save £50bn by 2050, with a pensions double lock saving £15bn
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said changes to the state pension triple lock will save £50bn by 2050. He also said a double lock on pensions will save £15bn.

squawks.headline: Healey says the Budget fully funds the defence investment plan
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said the government will fully fund the defence investment plan. No figures were given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Healey says local authorities will keep 100% of business rates by the end of the decade as he moves to devolve tax revenues
squawks.detail: In his Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the government is taking steps to devolve tax revenues. He said local authorities will retain all business rates by the end of the decade.

squawks.headline: Budget creates a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors in the Budget. No funding figure was given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Healey announces a founders relief within capital gains tax in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new founders relief in capital gains tax during the Budget speech. No further details were given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Budget sets out £140mn investment in strategic British AI companies
squawks.detail: The UK Budget includes £140mn of investment for strategic British AI firms, as announced during Chancellor Healey's speech.

squawks.headline: Healey allocates £20.4bn to the National Wealth Fund in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced £20.4bn for the National Wealth Fund in his Budget speech. He also announced a new British data centre covenant but gave no figures for it.

squawks.headline: Budget lifts the bank surcharge to 6% from 3% for 15 months starting in January
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey's 3 percentage point increase takes the bank surcharge to 6% from 3%. The extra charge applies for 15 months from January.

squawks.headline: Budget adds 3% to the bank surcharge
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey told parliament in the Budget that banks will pay an extra 3% on the bank surcharge.

squawks.headline: Healey raises tax rates on income from property and savings by 2 percentage points in the Budget
squawks.detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced higher tax rates on property and savings income, with the increase reported as 2 percentage points. He also said the threshold for business asset disposal relief is being cut.

squawks.headline: Healey drops the planned cash ISA change and keeps the £20k cash ISA limit for all ages
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey said the planned change to cash ISAs will not go ahead and the cash ISA limit stays at £20k for people of all ages.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine-Russia-US talks could take place as early as 10 November
squawks.detail: Ukrainian reports cite President Zelenskiy as saying that three-way negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the United States could start as early as 10 November.

squawks.headline: Budget lifts duty on gaming machines to 25% from 20% as Healey raises gambling taxes
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced higher gambling taxes in the Budget, including a rise in gaming machine duty to 25% from 20%. He also announced tighter rules on online marketplaces so that sellers cannot avoid paying VAT.

squawks.headline: Budget extends the 5p fuel duty cut to July 2027 and suspends tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced in the Budget that the 5p cut in fuel duty is extended to July 2027. He also announced that tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products are being suspended.

squawks.headline: OBR raises its 2027-28 UK borrowing forecast to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%
squawks.detail: The OBR's Budget forecast raises borrowing for 2027-28 to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%. It also has the deficit falling to 1.8% of GDP by 2031-32.

squawks.headline: OBR forecasts UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30, easing to 82.3% by 2030-31
squawks.detail: Budget forecasts put UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30. The OBR projects the ratio easing to 82.3% by 2030-31.

squawks.headline: Healey raises the national living wage by 3.9% in the Budget
squawks.detail: Chancellor Rachel Healey announced a 3.9% rise in the national living wage in his Budget statement.

squawks.headline: Healey exempts pensioners with income up to the full state pension from income tax under a new pension allowance
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new pension tax allowance in the Budget. Under it, pensioners whose income is no higher than the new full state pension will not pay income tax.

squawks.headline: Healey announces £100 energy payment for 20mn households at a cost of £2.6bn and extends electricity VAT cut to July 2027
squawks.detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said 20 million households will receive a £100 energy payment, at a cost of £2.6bn. He also extended the VAT cut on electricity bills to July 2027.

squawks.headline: Budget says £1 in every £13 of government spending goes on debt interest
squawks.detail: The government's Budget statement put debt interest at £1 in every £13 of public spending.

squawks.headline: Healey scraps the planned gas shippers obligation and moves more older renewables onto fixed-price contracts
squawks.detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey set out a new cost-controlled framework for energy bills, saying it aims to bring UK energy costs into line with Europe and reduce the effect of international gas prices on bills. He also said the UK remains committed to net zero by 2050.

squawks.headline: OBR cuts its 2027 UK GDP growth forecast to 1% from 1.6%
squawks.detail: The Budget forecasts cut UK GDP growth for 2027 to 1% from 1.6%, while 2026 growth was raised to 1.2% from 1.1%.

squawks.headline: OBR raises its 2026 UK GDP growth forecast to 1.2% from 1.1% in March
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey gave the upgraded OBR growth forecast in his Budget speech.

squawks.headline: Healey says fiscal headroom rises from £15bn to £22bn by 2030-31, with the rules met in the third forecast year
squawks.detail: The OBR's £15bn headroom against the current budget rule is down from £23.6bn in March and in line with the £15bn poll. The Chancellor said it climbs to £22bn by 2030-31 and that the fiscal rules will be met in the third year of the forecast.

squawks.headline: Healey rules out broad tax rises and cuts to public services in the Budget
squawks.detail: The Chancellor told Parliament his Budget aims to give families and businesses breathing space. He also said he will start a radical reform of energy to bring bills down.

squawks.headline: OBR forecasts UK borrowing at 4.2% of GDP in 2026-27, up from 3.6% previously, falling to 1.8% by 2031-32
squawks.detail: Chancellor Healey set out the OBR's Budget forecasts. They put public sector net financial liabilities at 83.2% of GDP in 2026-27, against 82.6% in March, and net financial debt at 82.3% of GDP in 2030-31.

squawks.headline: UK Budget puts fiscal headroom against the spending rule at £15bn, slightly below the £15.2bn expected
squawks.detail: The headroom figure was reported as Chancellor Healey presented the Budget on 28 October. It compares with an expected £15.2bn.

squawks.headline: Healey says he meets the fiscal rules and will use some headroom to absorb the Iran war, with debt interest up £14bn this year
squawks.detail: In his Budget speech, the Chancellor said he would keep cutting borrowing, would not raise tax on working people and had rejected broad-based tax rises. He said the OBR names the Middle East war as a key driver of its forecasts and that debt interest spending is £14bn higher this year.

squawks.headline: US preliminary wholesale inventories rise 0.6% m/m in September, above the 0.5% forecast
squawks.detail: US wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m in the preliminary September reading, against a forecast and a previous reading of 0.5%. Advance retail inventories excluding autos rose 0.4%, after 0.0% the month before.

squawks.headline: Healey opens Budget speech saying it rests on fiscal discipline and backs British business for growth
squawks.detail: As he opened the Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the Budget was for working people, would be built on fiscal discipline and would back British enterprise to drive growth. These were his opening remarks to the Commons.

squawks.headline: US advance goods trade deficit widens to $134.9bn, more than the $130.2bn forecast
squawks.detail: The advance US goods trade balance came in at -$134.9bn, against a forecast of -$130.2bn and -$132.07bn previously. In the same release, advance wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m, against a forecast of 0.5% and 0.5% previously.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham pledges to do all he can to secure a better EU deal for the UK
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said he would do everything he could to obtain an improved deal with the EU for the UK.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey begins presenting the UK Budget
squawks.detail: Reuters is carrying a live broadcast of Chancellor John Healey presenting the Budget on 28 October.

squawks.headline: US secured overnight financing rate rises to 3.95% on 27 October from 3.93%
squawks.detail: The US secured overnight financing rate was 3.95% on 27 October, compared with 3.93% on 26 October.

squawks.headline: Gulf stocks fall after an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery revives fears of Middle East escalation
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Gulf equity markets fell in early trade on Wednesday after an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter. The attack revived concerns that the conflict in the Middle East could escalate.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget bank tax rise is reported to be temporary, with the surcharge set below 8%
squawks.detail: Reports ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget say the higher tax on banks will be temporary and the bank surcharge will come in under 8%.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada is widely expected to raise its key rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday, its first hike in three years
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that most economists expect the Bank of Canada to raise its benchmark rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday. Economists see the move as protection against energy inflation spreading more widely.

squawks.headline: US regulator proposes rules to speed up LNG projects and expand export capacity
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that a US regulator on Wednesday proposed new rules to speed up liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity. The proposal is part of the Trump administration's wider push on energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Germany's 10-year Bund auction averages 3.37%, down from 3.58% last time; bid-to-cover falls to 1.1
squawks.detail: The average yield at Germany's 10-year Bund auction was 3.37%, compared with 3.58% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.1, down from 1.2.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak denies that Moscow is in talks with the US about American companies returning to Russian oil projects
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia is not negotiating with the US on a return to oil projects, TASS reported. This follows FT reports that the US was discussing Russian deals for American oil majors as part of the Ukraine peace talks.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Russia could also get security guarantees as part of a Ukraine peace deal, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Ukraine's president has acknowledged Moscow could receive security guarantees under a peace settlement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Senior Iranian official denies Qatar has made a new proposal to end hostilities with the US and calls its ideas unacceptable
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official said Qatar had not presented a fresh plan to end hostilities with the US, and that the ideas Qatar had put forward were unacceptable to Tehran. The official added that Iran's refusal to show flexibility on the nuclear issue is unchanged.

squawks.headline: Iran's president says the government is working to end the state of 'neither war nor peace'
squawks.detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said the government is working to get beyond the current state of neither war nor peace. Qatari mediators have given Iran a new draft deal, and Iran is expected to respond by the end of the week.

squawks.headline: Italian producer prices rise 3.6% m/m in September
squawks.detail: Italian producer prices rose 3.6% month on month in September, according to the data release.

squawks.headline: China's commerce minister notes recent EU trade restrictions on China and calls the EU an important trade partner
squawks.detail: China's commerce minister said in a statement that China has taken note of recent EU restrictive trade measures against it, and described China and the EU as important economic and trade partners.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget is set to focus on the cost of living, with modest measures and major decisions put off, Guardian reports
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Chancellor Healey will frame today's Budget around the cost of living crisis at what he calls a difficult moment. It says only modest policies are expected and that important decisions will be deferred.

squawks.headline: Qatari mediators give Iran a new draft deal with a seven-day timeline; Iran's response is expected by the end of the week
squawks.detail: An official briefed on the negotiations says Qatari mediators handed Iran the draft in Tehran on Sunday. Under the draft, both sides would take confidence-building steps every day, several countries would act as guarantors, and the timeline could begin early next week.

squawks.headline: China urges Germany and the EU to take a rational approach on trade and supply chains
squawks.detail: China's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that it is committed to keeping global industrial and supply chains stable and secure. It was responding to German Chancellor Merz's proposal for wider EU-Asia market access to counter trade restrictions.

squawks.headline: China says it will pay consumption subsidies faster to support spending
squawks.detail: China announced on 28 October that it will speed up subsidy payments aimed at lifting consumption. The report gave no amounts or timetable.

squawks.headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Moscow is preparing for Ukraine negotiations and hopes US dialogue can address the conflict's root causes
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Russia is in the preparation phase for negotiations on Ukraine. He also said Moscow hopes close dialogue with the US administration will help resolve the root causes of the conflict.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will not target Russian ships carrying diesel bound for the US
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Ukraine would not attack Russian vessels transporting diesel to the United States. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Brent and US crude futures rise more than $2 as supply risks return
squawks.detail: Brent and US crude futures were reported up by more than $2 a barrel, with the rise put down to renewed supply risks.

squawks.headline: German GfK consumer sentiment weakens to -30.8, below the -30.3 forecast
squawks.detail: The GfK consumer sentiment index for Germany came in at -30.8, compared with a forecast of -30.3 and -30.6 previously.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey abolishes standing charges on household gas bills
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the UK Chancellor is scrapping standing charges on gas bills and presents the change as making payments fairer. The report comes ahead of Wednesday's Budget.

squawks.headline: Bank of England is set to begin short-term precautionary monetary tightening in November, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Bank of England plans to start short-term precautionary tightening at its November meeting. The report came out before the UK Budget.

squawks.headline: Trump leaves open the possibility of further attacks on Iran after the election
squawks.detail: President Trump said he would not rule out more strikes on Iran once the US election is over.

squawks.headline: Trump says Ukraine peace efforts are progressing and he hopes to hold talks with Putin and Zelenskiy soon
squawks.detail: President Trump said efforts on Ukraine are moving forward and that he hopes to meet both Putin and Zelenskiy in the near future.

squawks.headline: Japan's 2-year government bond yield rises 2bp to 1.895%
squawks.detail: The 2-year JGB yield climbed 2bp to 1.895%, while the 5-year yield rose 3.5bp to 2.265%.

squawks.headline: Sterling edges lower towards $1.3300 ahead of the Budget and the Fed decision
squawks.detail: GBP/USD drifted towards 1.3300 in Asian trading, ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget and the Federal Reserve rate decision, according to an FX market report.

squawks.headline: Japan's 5-year government bond yield rises 3bp to 2.260%
squawks.detail: The yield on 5-year JGBs climbed 3bp to 2.260% in Asian trading on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: US signals a possible short, sharp escalation of the Iran conflict after the midterm elections, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Washington has signalled the possibility of a brief, intense escalation in the Iran conflict once the US midterm elections are over. The report gave no market reaction.

squawks.headline: RBNZ's Breman says the OCR is likely to rise above its earlier forecast path and tightening may reach restrictive levels
squawks.detail: At the briefing after the decision, the RBNZ Governor said the committee discussed raising the OCR track and the risk of a fall in AI-linked asset prices. She also said wage growth is still below levels consistent with the inflation target and that partial inflation and labour data will be key in the coming weeks.

squawks.headline: RBNZ Governor Breman says more rate hikes are probable at coming meetings and a lasting NZD fall could lift imported inflation
squawks.detail: The RBNZ Governor said policy may need to become more restrictive depending on the economy, and that the committee looked at market pricing and the fall in the New Zealand dollar. The Australian dollar rose 2% against the New Zealand dollar to NZ$1.2602, its highest since early 2013.

squawks.headline: Japanese government bond yields rise 4bp, with the 10-year at 2.825% and the 20-year at 3.635%
squawks.detail: The 20-year JGB yield rose 4bp to 3.635% and the 10-year rose 4bp to 2.825% in Asian trading on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey is set to present a cautious Budget on Wednesday amid bond market pressure, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Chancellor John Healey will set out a low-key Budget plan on Wednesday, aiming not to add to bond market pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham's new government.

squawks.headline: RBA's Bullock says inflation is unacceptably high and domestic demand still exceeds supply
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia Governor said Australian domestic demand remains above domestic supply and that inflation is too high.

squawks.headline: Israel's Netanyahu says the Iran mission is not complete and Israel will remove the threat together with Trump
squawks.detail: Speaking after Israel's elections, Prime Minister Netanyahu said Iran is weaker than ever but the campaign against it is not over and is only beginning.

squawks.headline: US military cost of the Iran war tops $47bn, Pentagon data show
squawks.detail: Pentagon data obtained by Reuters put US spending on the Iran war at more than $47bn so far, over 25% above the Defense Department's July estimate.

squawks.headline: RBA's Hunter says Australia is not expected to fall into recession
squawks.detail: RBA Assistant Governor Hunter said the central bank does not expect the Australian economy to slip into recession.

squawks.headline: RBNZ minutes say more OCR hikes are probable depending on the outlook; New Zealand dollar falls 1.4% to $0.5600
squawks.detail: The RBNZ minutes show Breman, Hansen, Gai and Williams voted to hold the OCR, while Conway, Gourley and Silk backed a hike. They also say international developments are adding to upside inflation risks and that high refined fuel prices and a weaker currency could spread inflation more widely. The New Zealand dollar fell 1.4% to $0.5600 after the hold.

squawks.headline: RBNZ holds its official cash rate at 2.75% on a 4-3 vote, against a forecast of 3%
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand left the OCR at 2.75%, while the forecast had been for 3%. It said all committee members agreed on the overall inflation outlook and that global factors are adding to inflation pressures.

squawks.headline: RBA's Bullock says the inflation outlook has worsened and the CPI data adds to upside risks; won't signal the board's decision
squawks.detail: The RBA Governor said inflation is now expected to run above the August projections, the labour market looks tighter than previously estimated and higher oil prices will add to inflation. Deputy Governor Hauser said the CPI figures were in line with expectations but still too high.

squawks.headline: Australian CPI rises 1.3% q/q in Q3, above 1.2% forecast; September annual rate climbs to 4.3%
squawks.detail: Q3 trimmed mean was 1.0% q/q, as forecast, and 3.7% y/y against a 3.6% forecast. Monthly CPI rose 0.8% m/m in September and 4.3% y/y against a 4.2% forecast, and the Australian dollar rose 0.4% to $0.7053 after the release.

squawks.headline: UK government weighs local investment and sustainability conditions for data centres in return for priority grid access
squawks.detail: City AM reports that ministers are examining the proposals ahead of Wednesday's Budget, after missing their own deadline for new planning rules.

squawks.headline: Healey puts energy reform at the centre of his Budget and pledges more support for businesses and households, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor will put energy reform at the centre of what it calls a 'do no harm' Budget. It also says he will pledge extra support for businesses, entrepreneurs and households.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey is set to reverse the cuts to cash ISA limits, FT reports
squawks.detail: According to the Financial Times, Chancellor Rachel Healey plans to reverse the earlier cuts to cash ISA allowances. The report came the evening before the Budget.

squawks.headline: Chile's central bank says it will set the rate path meeting by meeting and will monitor inflation persistence closely
squawks.detail: Chile's central bank says it will assess the future path of interest rates at each meeting and will watch closely for signs that shocks are passing through more widely or that inflation is persisting. It says the economy may regain momentum by 2027, but current weakness could last longer than expected.

squawks.headline: US sells first Venezuelan crude cargo, received at no cost, to Citgo and Exxon Mobil, White House official says
squawks.detail: A White House official says the US government received the first Venezuelan crude cargo from NABEP at no cost under an August deal. The official says the cargo has been sold to Citgo Petroleum and Exxon Mobil.

squawks.headline: Kremlin's Peskov says the local Ukraine ceasefire deal at first covered only a halt in fighting around one town
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the ceasefire agreement originally provided for a period of quiet around a single town. Earlier reports said the local ceasefire had been extended beyond Oleshky in the Kherson region.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey is preparing a £50 cut to household gas bills, Telegraph reports
squawks.detail: The Telegraph reports that Chancellor Healey is preparing to cut household gas bills by £50. The report comes ahead of the Budget, which is due tomorrow.

squawks.headline: ECB authorises Intesa Sanpaolo to take control of Monte dei Paschi ahead of its €32bn takeover offer
squawks.detail: Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's biggest bank, said on Tuesday that it had received European Central Bank authorisation to take control of Monte dei Paschi di Siena, Reuters reports. The approval is a major step towards launching its €32bn ($36bn) offer.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says Russia cannot export diesel at present and the Iran war has come at a cost
squawks.detail: The US Energy Secretary also said the Constellation Energy deal will add 1.1 gigawatts of capacity. These remarks came alongside earlier comments on US LNG exports and on flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: Trump to announce looser rules on methane leaks from oil companies, Washington Post reports
squawks.detail: The Washington Post reports that President Trump will announce relaxed regulations on methane leaks from oil firms.

squawks.headline: US and Russia propose a post-war oil venture off the Sakhalin coast, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the US and Russia have put forward a joint oil venture off Sakhalin to follow the end of the Ukraine war. Earlier, the FT reported that Russian deals for American oil majors were being discussed in the peace talks.

squawks.headline: US is discussing Russian deals for American oil majors as part of Ukraine peace talks, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Washington is discussing deals in Russia for US oil majors within the Ukraine peace negotiations. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the suspension of sanctions on Russia is temporary and the US is ramping up LNG exports
squawks.detail: In remarks on CNBC, which have now ended, US Energy Secretary Wright also said Russia cannot currently export diesel.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says more refined products are moving out through the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said refined product flows from the Strait of Hormuz have risen. He did not give any figures, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Treasury accepts $6bn of offers in a buyback of 2046-2056 coupons, taking the maximum from $10.746bn offered
squawks.detail: The US Treasury received $10.746bn of offers in a buyback aimed at coupon securities maturing between 2046 and 2056. It accepted $6bn, the maximum, across 6 of the 35 eligible issues.

squawks.headline: Fiscal devolution roadmap on mayors' revenue-raising and spending is due to be published in tomorrow's Budget
squawks.detail: The Institute for Government says the government's fiscal devolution roadmap will be unveiled in the Budget on 28 October. It will set out changes to how mayors raise and spend money.

squawks.headline: Canada and the UAE sign a comprehensive trade deal
squawks.detail: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi signed the deal at a joint signing ceremony.

squawks.headline: Trump says petrol and diesel prices will soon fall sharply as Venezuelan oil shipments begin
squawks.detail: In posts on Truth Social, the US President said the Venezuelan cargo is the first of billions of barrels to come. He also said US energy output from Alaska to Venezuela has made the Western Hemisphere the world's energy capital.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Venezuelan oil cargo the US is taking is only the first shipment
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the shipment of Venezuelan oil bound for the US is the first of more to come. One report gave the cargo as 1 million barrels and another as 100 million barrels; the earlier blotter entry carried 1 million barrels.

squawks.headline: US Treasury sells $70bn of 5-year notes at a 4.845% high yield with a 0.4bp tail; bid-to-cover 2.33
squawks.detail: The high yield compares with 5.033% at the previous 5-year sale, and bid-to-cover rose to 2.33 from 2.210. Indirect bidders took 60.0%, directs 29.4% and primary dealers 10.6%.

squawks.headline: US 5-year Treasury when-issued yield is 4.841% ahead of the $70bn auction
squawks.detail: Ahead of the US Treasury's $70bn 5-year note auction, the when-issued yield was quoted at 4.841%.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Putin the region can resolve its problems without the US
squawks.detail: Iran's president made the remarks during talks with Russia's president in Moscow, Tasnim reports.

squawks.headline: Russian refineries' crude processing is up 25% since drone attacks halted in mid-October, Reuters sources say
squawks.detail: Reuters sources say crude runs at Russian refineries have risen 25% since drone attacks stopped in mid-October. Earlier, Russia's Novak said refineries were restarting quickly.

squawks.headline: Kremlin's Peskov says it is too early to tell whether the Putin call with Stubb and Støre will affect the Abu Dhabi talks
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin's phone call with Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre could, in some circumstances, influence contacts in Abu Dhabi, but that it is premature to say so yet.

squawks.headline: EU leans on allies as a shortfall in Ukraine funding approaches, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the EU is pressing allied governments over an approaching gap in funding for Ukraine. The report gives no figures.

squawks.headline: Melania Trump says the local Ukraine ceasefire has begun and now extends beyond Oleshky within the Kherson region
squawks.detail: US First Lady Melania Trump said the localised ceasefire in Ukraine has started and has been widened beyond Oleshky to cover more of the Kherson region. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says a Russia-Ukraine leaders' meeting would only make sense once negotiations are complete
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said contact between the Russian and Ukrainian leaders would be appropriate after the negotiation process has finished, to sign documents. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide says Putin told Stubb and Støre that Zelenskyy may visit Moscow and security would be guaranteed
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said Putin confirmed in his call with Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre that Zelenskyy may visit Moscow. According to Ushakov, Putin said all necessary conditions for such a visit, including security, would be provided.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US will accept 1 million barrels of Venezuelan oil and plans to visit a tanker carrying it in Texas
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks in comments carried live on Tuesday. He said he expects to visit a tanker in Texas that is carrying Venezuelan oil.

squawks.headline: US Treasury sells $54bn of 52-week bills at a 4.29% high yield, down from 4.400% previously; bid-to-cover 3.15
squawks.detail: The US 52-week bill auction cleared at a high yield of 4.29%, against 4.400% at the previous sale, with bid-to-cover of 3.15 against 3.070. 65.33% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

squawks.headline: Poland's energy minister expects a schedule for releasing oil stockpiles to be ready by the end of November
squawks.detail: Polish Energy Minister Motyka said the timetable for releasing oil from stockpiles should be finalised by the end of November. No volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says the Oleshky ceasefire could serve as a confidence-building step in peace talks
squawks.detail: Ukraine's foreign minister also said Kyiv coordinated the call that the Finnish and Norwegian leaders held with Putin.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov expects the Ukraine conflict to continue and probably escalate; says the Finland and Norway call with Putin offered…
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Europe wants a role in the negotiations, and that the Finnish and Norwegian leaders brought nothing new to their call with Putin, according to Interfax. He also said the Russia-US diesel deal is a purely commercial agreement with no extra conditions.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak offers to help Gulf states restore oil refineries and to supply technology and equipment
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia stands ready to help Persian Gulf countries restore their oil refineries, including by providing technology and equipment. He also said Russian refineries are bringing units back online quickly after maintenance, using mostly Russian-made equipment.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Russia-US Arctic projects could cover gas fields or joint LNG, and refineries are restarting quickly
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said possible Russia-US projects in the Arctic could involve developing gas fields or taking part in joint LNG projects. He also said Russian refineries are bringing units back online very quickly after maintenance.

squawks.headline: Finland's Stubb says the Putin call was prepared together with Ukraine and the US
squawks.detail: Russian media report that Finnish President Stubb said his phone call with Putin on the Ukraine war was prepared jointly with Ukraine and the United States.

squawks.headline: Brent falls to its intraday low and trades near $114 a barrel
squawks.detail: Market reports say oil fell to its low of the session, with Brent trading close to $114 a barrel.

squawks.headline: Dallas Fed services activity index rises to 4.0 in October, against a -2.9 forecast
squawks.detail: The Dallas Fed's services activity index for October came in at 4.0. The forecast was -2.9 and the previous reading was -1.8.

squawks.headline: Finland's Stubb says he passed on Ukraine's messages to Putin and that the US and Ukraine asked Finland and Norway to do more
squawks.detail: Finnish President Stubb said he relayed messages from Ukraine during his call with Putin. He said the US and Ukraine had asked Norway and Finland to take a more active role in efforts to end the war.

squawks.headline: US consumers' 12-month inflation expectations ease to 5.8% in October but stay elevated, Conference Board says
squawks.detail: The Conference Board's October consumer confidence report puts consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations at 5.8%, lower than the previous month. It adds that consumers still expect interest rates to be higher over the next 12 months.

squawks.headline: US new home sales fall 0.6% m/m, a smaller drop than the 4.5% decline forecast
squawks.detail: US new home sales fell 0.6% on the month, against a forecast fall of 4.5%. The previous month showed a 6.4% rise.

squawks.headline: US Conference Board consumer confidence jumps to 91.7 in October, well above the 81.0 forecast
squawks.detail: The Conference Board's October consumer confidence index came in at 91.7 against a consensus of 81.0. September's reading was revised up to 84.2 from 81.9.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's defence ministry in Riyadh
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis say they hit the Saudi defence ministry in the capital with a ballistic missile, following their earlier claim of a strike on the Ras Tanura refinery. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attack.

squawks.headline: Economists' poll lifts global growth forecasts to 3.0% for 2026 and 3.2% for 2027; 2027 inflation views raised for 31 of 50 economies
squawks.detail: A poll of economists puts global growth at 3.0% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, up from 2.9% and 3.1% in the July poll. Forecasts for 2027 inflation were raised for 31 of 50 major economies compared with July.

squawks.headline: UK minister Reynolds says EU uncertainty is hurting British business and the long-term relationship must be settled
squawks.detail: The FT reports that minister Reynolds said uncertainty over the UK's relations with the EU is damaging British business and the long-term relationship needs resolving. He spoke ahead of new UK-EU talks.

squawks.headline: US set to approve three more wind projects, Punchbowl reports
squawks.detail: Punchbowl reports that the US administration will approve three more wind power projects. No other details were given.

squawks.headline: US Case-Shiller 20-city house prices rise 2.65% y/y in August, above 2.61% forecast; FHFA index up 0.3% m/m
squawks.detail: The S&P Case-Shiller 20-city index rose 2.65% year on year in August, against a 2.61% forecast and 2.5% previously. The FHFA house price index rose 0.3% month on month, against a 0.2% forecast, and its annual rate eased to 2.4% from 2.6%.

squawks.headline: British Business Bank and National Wealth Fund set for a boost in Healey's Budget, Observer reports
squawks.detail: The Observer reports that public finance institutions, including the British Business Bank and the National Wealth Fund, are due to get extra support in the Chancellor's Budget. The report gives no figures.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they pushed back an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb strait
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis say they repelled a Saudi-led advance near the Bab el-Mandeb strait and fired ballistic missiles and heavy weapons at the advancing forces. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield edges up 0.86bp to 4.995% after US data; 30-year flat at 5.304%
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields moved after the release of US economic data. The 10-year yield was last up 0.86bp at 4.995%, while the 30-year yield was last unchanged at 5.304%.

squawks.headline: Norway's Støre says his call with Putin on the Ukraine war revealed big differences
squawks.detail: Norway's prime minister said there were big differences with the Russian president during their call on the war in Ukraine. Finland's president also took part in the call.

squawks.headline: US durable goods orders rise 1.8%, just below the 1.9% forecast; core orders up 0.5%
squawks.detail: US durable goods orders rose 1.8% against a 1.9% forecast, after -0.1% the previous month. Core durable goods rose 0.5% against a 0.6% forecast, after 0.2% the previous month.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation estimates fiscal headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation estimates that headroom against the fiscal rules will have fallen to around £12bn in 2029-30 before any Budget measures. It says Chancellor John Healey would need £18bn of headroom to keep a buffer equivalent to the one Rachel Reeves had.

squawks.headline: Poland's Tusk says Finland's Stubb described the European position on the Abu Dhabi talks as moderately optimistic
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Finland's president told him, after his call with Putin, that Europe is moderately optimistic about the Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Downing Street rules out a UK return to EU free movement during the current parliament
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister's spokeswoman said the UK will not return to EU free movement in this parliament. She added that the coming UK-EU summit may take concrete steps but these will not be enough.

squawks.headline: Norway's Støre says his views on Ukraine match those of the coalition of the willing
squawks.detail: Norway's prime minister made the remark after his phone call with Putin, held with Finland's Stubb, about efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Norway's Støre says Moscow appears to be preparing thoroughly for the Abu Dhabi talks and calls for de-escalation of the Ukraine war
squawks.detail: Norway's prime minister said his call with Putin lasted 90 minutes and that his impression was that Moscow is preparing thoroughly for the Abu Dhabi meeting. He also said efforts must be made to de-escalate the war in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly employment change slows to 16.75K from 18.5K
squawks.detail: ADP's weekly US private-sector employment estimate showed a gain of 16.75K, down from 18.5K the previous week. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Putin calls for ending ongoing conflicts and lifting sanctions to be considered, and warns against overdoing the green agenda
squawks.detail: Russian President Putin said ending current conflicts and removing sanctions should be considered, and that the green agenda should not be taken too far. He made the remarks in the same appearance as his earlier comments on the gas market.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia is open to gas cooperation and is looking at working with US partners, including in the Arctic
squawks.detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia is open to cooperation in the gas sector and is looking into possible joint work with partners from the US, including in the Arctic. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Putin warns that trying to shut Russia out of the global gas market has serious consequences and urges gas exporters to coordinate routes
squawks.detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin said global natural gas prices have risen sharply but may fall again, and that gas supply needs to increase. He proposed that gas-exporting countries work together to optimise export and transport routes.

squawks.headline: Putin describes the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines as direct acts of terrorism
squawks.detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin called the attacks on the Nord Stream gas pipelines direct acts of terrorism. Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Russia was ready to resume gas supplies to Europe. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Oleshky ceasefire will run until 1 November, says senior Ukrainian official
squawks.detail: A senior Ukrainian official said the local ceasefire in Oleshky will remain in place until 1 November. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Three Russian diesel tankers head for the US, one of them under sanctions, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that three tankers of Russian diesel are sailing to the US under the Trump-Putin fuel deal, and that one of them is under sanctions. The FT says the arrangement exposes the companies involved to legal threats from Congress.

squawks.headline: QatarEnergy extends force majeure on LNG supplies to Italy's Edison through December
squawks.detail: QatarEnergy has extended the force majeure on its LNG deliveries to Italian energy company Edison until the end of December, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Moscow can redirect and sell all its gas elsewhere if Europe turns down supplies
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia could reroute its gas and sell all of it if European countries reject supplies. He had earlier said Moscow was ready to resume gas deliveries to Europe.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Moscow is ready to resume gas supplies to European countries if they want them
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia was prepared to restart gas deliveries to Europe should European countries wish. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says a fourth tanker of Russian diesel under the Russia-US deal leaves on 28 October
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said a fourth tanker of Russian diesel under the Russia-US diesel deal will depart on 28 October. He said three more tankers are currently en route.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi forces said they hit the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province with a ballistic missile and that the strike caused large fires. Saudi Arabia had earlier said it had contained a fire near the oil hub after an attack.

squawks.headline: UK sells £4.5bn of 5-year gilts at an average yield of 5.036%, the highest since 2008
squawks.detail: The UK sold £4.5bn of 5-year debt at an average yield of 5.036%, the highest since 2008. New OBR forecasts are due tomorrow; in March the OBR forecast that debt servicing would soon cost 3.8% of GDP.

squawks.headline: Iran's supreme leader calls for conditions to be met to end the war and discusses Hormuz management with Rezaee
squawks.detail: Iran's supreme leader called for the conditions for ending the war to be met. Separately, he discussed national unity and the management of the Strait of Hormuz with Rezaee. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Putin told Stubb and Støre peace needs Russia's interests met in full and EU and NATO policies prolong the war
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders of Finland and Norway that peace can only come if Russia's interests are taken into account fully and without conditions. It said he also told them that confrontational EU and NATO policies are dragging out the conflict.

squawks.headline: German 2-year Schatz auction clears at 3.08% with bid-to-cover of 1.3
squawks.detail: The German 2-year Schatz auction produced an average yield of 3.08%, compared with 3.1% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.3, up from 1.1 last time.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Russia-US-Ukraine talks will resume in Abu Dhabi in November to address postwar security
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the three-way talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine will restart in Abu Dhabi in November. It said the talks will cover postwar security arrangements.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Putin, Stubb and Støre discussed the Oleshky ceasefire and agreed to keep direct contact
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the leaders of Finland and Norway requested the call, which covered settling the war in Ukraine, the Oleshky ceasefire and upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi, TASS reported. Denmark's prime minister was reported as saying she is very sceptical about Norway and Finland talking to Putin.

squawks.headline: Qatar's foreign ministry says Iran must halt threats to Gulf states and reopen the Strait of Hormuz for mediation to work
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for Qatar's foreign ministry said Iran needs to demonstrate good intentions and stop threatening Arab Gulf states. The spokesperson also said Tehran must open the Strait of Hormuz for mediation efforts to succeed.

squawks.headline: Gulf stock markets rise after Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iran in Tehran to ease escalation
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that major Gulf stock markets rose in early trade on Tuesday. The gains came a day after senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran to try to ease military escalation.

squawks.headline: Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre hold phone call with Putin on efforts to end the war in Ukraine
squawks.detail: Finland's presidential office says President Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Støre started the call with President Putin to discuss Russia's war against Ukraine and diplomatic efforts to end it. The office says the call related to upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says no breaches of the Oleshky ceasefire have been reported so far
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said on 27 October that no violations of the Oleshky ceasefire agreement with Ukraine had been reported so far. It also said no date has yet been set for US-Ukraine talks in the UAE, TASS reports.

squawks.headline: Iran's Gulf strait authority says Sinokor Shipping vessels will face legal action from 1 November
squawks.detail: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said all vessels belonging to Sinokor Shipping will be met with legal action starting 1 November.

squawks.headline: OPEC+ reportedly set to keep oil output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting
squawks.detail: Sources say OPEC+ is expected to hold its oil production targets steady when it meets on Sunday.

squawks.headline: French finance minister Lescure says France must answer protesters without adding to spending
squawks.detail: In an FT interview, Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the government can find creative solutions without widening the budget deficit. He also said an unwinding of carry trades had added to pressure on short-dated French debt during this month's volatility.

squawks.headline: Eurozone M3 money supply grows 3.5% y/y, slightly above the 3.4% forecast; lending growth holds steady
squawks.detail: Eurozone annual M3 growth was 3.5%, unchanged from the previous reading and against a 3.4% forecast. Loans to non-financial firms grew 4.2% and loans to households grew 3.1%, both the same as the previous month.

squawks.headline: France-Germany 10-year yield spread widens 6bp to 160bp
squawks.detail: The gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields widened by 6bp to 160bp on Tuesday morning, according to a market wire.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia says it has contained a fire near the Ras Tanura oil hub after an attack
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia reports that a fire near its Ras Tanura oil hub, which broke out after an attack, has been contained. The report gave no details on damage to oil supply and no market reaction.

squawks.headline: UK business minister says Britain and EU are making progress on concerns over the bloc's proposed 'Made in Europe' rules
squawks.detail: UK business minister Jonathan Reynolds said on Tuesday that London and Brussels are working through concerns over the EU's planned 'Made in Europe' rules, according to Reuters. The rules have caused uncertainty for UK manufacturers and investors.

squawks.headline: Merz says a US-Russia-China understanding on Ukraine that leaves out Kyiv would be unacceptable
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz, speaking in Singapore, said it would be wholly unacceptable for the US, Russia and China to try to reach an understanding without Ukraine's involvement.

squawks.headline: French consumer confidence drops to 80 in October, its lowest since June 2013
squawks.detail: France's October consumer confidence index came in at 80, against a forecast of 85 and down from 86 in September. It is the lowest reading since June 2013.

squawks.headline: French retailers will not replenish the diesel stocks they have released, Politico reports
squawks.detail: Politico reports that retailers in France do not plan to refill diesel stocks that have been released. The report gives no volumes and no market reaction.

squawks.headline: China's foreign ministry urges EU not to misuse trade remedy tools as Brussels plans trade measures
squawks.detail: Responding to EU plans for trade measures, China's foreign ministry said it regards China-EU trade ties as a partnership. It said it hopes the EU will not abuse its trade remedy tools.

squawks.headline: Japan's 30-year JGB yield rises 1.5bp to 3.820%
squawks.detail: Japan's 30-year government bond yield rose 1.5bp to 3.820% in early trading on 27 October.

squawks.headline: China's December 30-year government bond futures rise 0.4% to a record 118.56
squawks.detail: China's 30-year government bond futures for December delivery rose 0.4% to a record high of 118.56.

squawks.headline: India's oil minister says Washington is not pressing India to cut its Russian crude imports
squawks.detail: India's oil minister said the US is not putting pressure on India to reduce its imports of Russian crude. He also said US cargoes now make up 67% of India's LPG imports.

squawks.headline: Brazil's real suffers its worst day in more than 25 years as Lula faces calls for budget cuts, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that investor worries about how the economy is being managed drove falls in the real and the Bovespa index after the president's re-election.

squawks.headline: Bank of England orders Section 166 review of Revolut's product approval processes, FT reports
squawks.detail: According to the FT, the order was made earlier this year and focuses on risks from the rapid launch of new financial products.

squawks.headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama says government is ready to take decisive action in the currency market
squawks.detail: Katayama said officials are watching market moves with heightened urgency, that the yen should move in line with fundamentals, and that clear communication aims to keep market confidence in the yen and in the Takaichi administration's fiscal policy.

squawks.headline: HSBC third-quarter profit rises 32% and the bank announces a buyback of up to $1bn
squawks.detail: The bank said higher rates supported net interest income, and it expects banking NII of at least $46bn in 2026. Pre-tax profit of $9.63bn and revenue of $18.6bn were both below estimates.

squawks.headline: Taiwan central bank calls its policy stance tightening and forecasts 5.82% GDP growth for next year
squawks.detail: The central bank named geopolitical risks and climate conditions as the main uncertainties for inflation, said bank loan quality was stable, and reported that the Taiwan dollar fell 1.25% against the US dollar in the first half.

squawks.headline: Japan corporate services prices rise 3.7% y/y in September
squawks.detail: Data published on Tuesday show Japan's corporate services price index, a key gauge of service-sector inflation, up 3.7% on a year earlier in September. Reuters says the figure points to mounting price pressures.

squawks.headline: China industrial profits rise 14.4% y/y in September, up from 4.2% in August; year-to-date growth eases to 15.5%
squawks.detail: China's statistics bureau says industrial profits for January to September are up 15.5% on a year earlier, compared with 15.7% for the year to August. September profits alone rose 14.4% year on year.

squawks.headline: People's Bank of China injects 1 trillion yuan through overnight reverse repos
squawks.detail: China's central bank said in a statement that it had added 1 trillion yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repurchase operations.

squawks.headline: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in Oleshky takes effect; Russia suspends strikes on Kherson
squawks.detail: The local ceasefire in Oleshky came into force, according to reports. Russia's Defence Ministry said it has suspended strikes on Ukraine's Kherson.
